findings.title: Every live region that holds a field redraws only after focus leaves it: the Planner, the Table, a GM's Remnant card and the Mastermind's Hope box
findings.surface: Investigation - the Map view (the planner) and the Table view; A GM's card of a Remnant; The Mastermind window
findings.what_happens: keepLive's rule 1 defers every rebuild while focus sits in a text input, textarea or select inside the region and answers it at the focusout that leaves the region. The Investigation dashboard's region is the whole Table and the whole Map, and on the Map every node is open by default (caseMapAllOpen), so a GM planning a case has a field under the caret almost all the time: a player's find, an Analyze, another GM's Save or a reshape ruling reach the window only when the GM clicks out of the field. The same holds on a GM's Remnant card (name, texts and two selects inside the region) and on the Mastermind window's Hope box (donor select, amount). The owner's standing rule of 20.11.2026 ('Zawsze odswiezamy okna od razu przy zmianie') names the Planner as its example.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM types a deduction's text in an open node of the Planner while a player's Observe gives them a Key Remnant's Truth Bullet; the node's 'found by', the reach and the summary keep the old reading until the GM clicks somewhere outside the field.
findings.expected: The read-out parts redraw at once whatever has focus, with the field being typed in kept as it is (rule 2 already carries dirty fields and marks a field the world moved under, live.mjs:530-549).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a path that forces the region while focus is in it: live.refresh() is forced (live.mjs:293) but only the GM's own filter, fold and view switch call it (investigation.mjs:2307, 2350-2351, 2415-2416); the trial console's tick forces its own region, which holds no field. keepFresh has no focus rule but the dashboard uses it only for the footer's body button (investigation.mjs:2386-2387). Rule 1 is a recorded design (live.mjs:32-37, 'Not preserve the caret - wait') written before the owner's rule of 20.11.2026, so this is the design meeting the new rule, not a slip; the conflict is for the owner. No base run or probe-43 file was there to read.
findings.probe: Open the Investigation dashboard on the Map with all nodes open, focus a node's text field, then on a player's page run an Observe that creates a Truth Bullet of a placed Remnant; read the node's holders line before and two seconds after, then blur the field and read it again.

findings.title: The Investigation dashboard does not hear the Truth Bullets' answer keys: 'found by', Who has what and the Map's reach stay as drawn without a key that lands after its item
findings.surface: Investigation - the Table view; Investigation - the Map view
findings.what_happens: Every 'found by', the Who has what tab, the Map's holders and autopsyIssued read a Truth Bullet's answer key through secretOf, which is the GM store bulletStore. The dashboard watches actors, items and six other stores, not bulletStore. createTruthBullet creates the item first and writes the key after more awaits; on a second GM the item arrives from the server and the key through the GMs' exchange. A redraw that runs on createItem before the key is in reads the bullet as a find of nothing, and the key's own arrival (a clientSettingChanged of bulletStore) wakes nothing. Later amendments of a key (analyzedText after an Analyze, the faint mark) are not heard either.
findings.failure_scenario: With two GMs, a player's Observe makes a Truth Bullet of a Key Remnant on the primary; the second GM's open dashboard redraws on the item and then shows that Remnant as found by nobody until some other write redraws it.
findings.expected: bulletStore among the dashboard's watched stores, as remnantStore and keyPlanStore are.
findings.refutation_tried: Read every source of 'found by' (findersByAnyRemnant, evidenceByStudent, caseReach, autopsyIssued): all go through secretOf. Checked listenFor (live.mjs:346-351): only the stores named are heard. On the writing GM the key usually lands inside the 120 ms debounce (config.mjs:439), so the single-GM case may draw right; the second GM's order (item before key) is read from the write order, not measured - the gap in the watch is read, the visible timing is not.
findings.probe: Two GM pages with the dashboard open on the second; on the primary `game.drpg` road that issues a Truth Bullet of a placed trace; on the second read the trace row's found-by cell at 1 s and 5 s.

findings.title: With no floor open the trial console's Reveal list hears none of its sources: a Key placed, found or revealed, or another GM's Key plan write
findings.what_happens: The Missing Key Remnants list and 'Left to reveal' are built from missingKeyRows (keyPlanStore, the ledger, trace tokens and the finders read off Truth Bullet items and their keys) and keyRevealRecord (keyPlanStore). The console's region watches the module's settings, three hooks and blackenedStore and deathStore; the one-second tick runs only while a floor is open. In discussion, during the vote or before the verdict nothing in that list redraws it. controls-01-trial-console-6 records the case of a Reveal; the same holds for any other write of those sources.
findings.failure_scenario: In the trial's discussion a second GM fills the name of a Key slot in the planner; the first GM's console still lists that slot under its old empty name until a ballot or a setting moves.
findings.expected: The console's region hears keyPlanStore, remnantStore and items, as the schema beside it hears keyPlanStore (case-trial.mjs:126).
findings.refutation_tried: A press of a stale row re-reads missingKeys and refuses ('That Key Remnant is not missing'), so nothing is revealed wrong (trial-floor-ui.mjs:1060-1065); that keeps it a nit. Same root as controls-01-trial-console-6, filed for the sources that finding does not name.
findings.probe: In a running trial with no floor, open the console; on a second GM write a Key slot's name through the planner; read `.drpg-reveal-list` on the first GM two seconds later.

findings.title: The Findings window is drawn once: a Finding a zone mode writes at its end, or another GM's, is not in the open window while the console beside it counts it
findings.what_happens: The window draws findingsNow() (trialProgress.findings) at its opening and again only after one of its own Edit, Delete or Confirm presses. A Straw Poll or Logic Dive that ends writes its Finding into the trial record in the record's own step; the console's 'Findings (n)' button, in its live region, counts it at once, and the Findings window the GM opened from that button keeps the old list with no row for it.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM keeps the Findings window open over the console during a Straw Poll; the poll ends with a clear side, the console's button reads 'Findings (2)', the window still lists one and has no 'Monokuma confirms' for the new one.
findings.expected: The list redraws on the trial record, as the console's count does.
findings.refutation_tried: Read the render hook: one click listener and no keepLive, keepFresh or hook (trial-zones-ui.mjs:399-413). git grep openFindings: no other code redraws the window. The Add footer closes it, so the GM's own add is not the case.
findings.probe: `game.drpg.openFindings()` during a Straw Poll, let the poll's 60 s run out with one side ahead; count `.drpg-findings-list li` against the console's Findings button text.

findings.title: The side-pick window keeps the first question's words and answers on its buttons while a Logic Dive moves on, and stays after the mode ends
findings.surface: Side-pick window of a participant with no token in the hall
findings.what_happens: offerSidePick draws zone.question and the two answers into the body and the buttons' labels once, keyed by mode and openedAt. A Logic Dive's next question replaces zone.question and zone.answers and keeps openedAt, so the window (with no watch and no close) stands on question 1 while question 2 is on the floor; its press sends only actorId and side, which the primary applies to the zone now. In a Straw Poll it stays after the vote phase ends and a press is refused.
findings.failure_scenario: A player with no token in the hall leaves the side-pick window open through Logic Dive question 1 and presses 'Zone A: Yes' during question 2, whose Zone A answer is a different one: the side counts for question 2.
findings.expected: The window follows the floor: its question and labels redraw with the question, and it closes when the mode or the vote phase ends, as the turn prompts close (trial-prompt.mjs:201-206).
findings.refutation_tried: Read offerSidePick whole: no render hook, no interval. Checked phase() keeps openedAt (zone-machine.mjs:135), so no second window opens for question 2 (which is also controls-02-trial-zones-verdict-1's root). Whether the primary takes a late side for the next question was read from the request's two fields, not from sideOnPrimary's body.
findings.probe: A player's page with no hall token, a Logic Dive of two questions; leave the window open past question 1's 60 s; read `.drpg-side-pick` text and its buttons' labels against the floor's zone.question.

findings.title: A ballot window left open stays after the vote is closed and counted; Cast is then answered 'The vote has moved on'
findings.surface: The ballot a player gets: 'Who did it?'
findings.what_happens: castBallot closes an older ballot window when a newer ballot arrives (remind, resend, restart). Nothing closes it when the vote is closed and counted: closeVote asks the primary and sends no packet to the ballot's browser, and the window has no watch of the trial record.
findings.failure_scenario: A player who walked away from the table comes back to the ballot still on screen after the GM counted the vote, picks a name, presses Cast and reads that the vote has moved on.
findings.expected: The ballot closes when its round is no longer open, as the turn prompts close with their turn.
findings.refutation_tried: git grep 'drpg-ballot' and closeOpen: the only close is vote.mjs:817. The refusal is said (vote.mjs:914), so no vote is lost; the window is only wrong about whether it still counts.
findings.probe: With a player's ballot window open, `game.drpg` close and count on the GM; read whether `.drpg-ballot` is still rendered on the player's page five seconds later.

findings.title: The Mastermind window reads the pick, the lair and the Hope box's recipient once: another GM's change is not shown, and Apply writes the drawn lair back over theirs
findings.what_happens: The 'who' and 'lair' selects, whether the Give Hope fieldset is drawn and the Mastermind it gives to are read from mastermindStore at the opening; only the Hope box is a live region (actors and drpgDespairOwedChanged). applyMastermindChoice compares the submitted pick with the Mastermind drawn at the opening, but the lair with the store as it is now, so a window whose pick still names the drawn one writes its drawn lair over a lair another GM set meanwhile.
findings.failure_scenario: Two GMs: one moves the Mastermind's lair to the Library while the other has the Mastermind window open on the Gym; the second presses Apply without touching anything and the lair is the Gym again.
findings.expected: The selects follow mastermindStore, and Apply writes only what was changed from what was drawn, as Season setup's scenes part does (trial-scene.mjs:1617).
findings.refutation_tried: Traced Apply: who === current.id skips the pick, then the lair branch writes setMastermindLair(result.lair) whenever it differs from readStore().room (mastermind.mjs:559-580). The window is GM-only and alreadyOpen keeps one per browser, so the case needs two GMs; mastermindStore.whenHydrated (:607) settles only the opening.
findings.probe: Two GM pages; open the Mastermind window on one; on the other `game.drpg.setMastermindLair('<room>')`; press Apply on the first unchanged; read mastermindStore's room.

Nothing hears the sceneRoles setting, a scene's regions or the cast. Apply writes only the fields changed from what was drawn, so nothing is written back.

findings.title: The turn prompts' seconds are drawn once: 'Your turn (60 s)' and the volunteers' count never move, and a GM's +30 s or -30 s does not reach them
findings.surface: the speaker's prompt - 'Your turn ({seconds} s)'; the volunteers' question - 'Closing Argument' (I'll sum up?)
findings.what_happens: promptTurn writes the turn's seconds (the Closing's seconds left) into the title, and promptClaim the seconds left into the body, once. Their 500 ms watches read the floor only to close the window. The bar's +30 s / -30 s moves the floor's startedAt, so the turn runs longer or shorter than the number on the window says.
findings.failure_scenario: In a Testimony the GM gives the speaker +30 s; the speaker's window still says 'Your turn (60 s)' while the HUD's clock counts the longer turn.
findings.expected: The seconds on the prompts follow the floor, as the console's do.
findings.refutation_tried: Read both windows' render hooks: the intervals close and do nothing else. The HUD's own readout does count (hud-elapsed.mjs), so the player has a right number elsewhere; that keeps it a nit.
findings.probe: A player's page in a Testimony with the prompt open; GM presses +30 s; read the prompt's title and the HUD's seconds.

findings.title: The held Key fee's card keeps 'Charge the Key fee' on every GM after the fee has been charged
findings.surface: The held Key fee's card (a whisper to the GMs)
findings.what_happens: wireChargeHeld removes the button on the browser that pressed it. Nothing redraws the card when trialProgress.keysCharged is written - by another GM's press or by the trial's own charge - so every other GM's card still offers the charge; a reload draws it again. A press then says the fee is done.

findings.title: The vote window and the console's vote lines do not follow a student's sheet: an owner or a Monocub / not-in-the-class flag changed while they stand
findings.surface: the vote window - 'The vote'; the Class Trial console
findings.what_happens: trialParticipants, which both windows print through ballotRecipients and pendingVoters, reads each student's ownership and its Monocub and not-in-the-class flags (as the GMs hold them, flagsHeldNow). Neither window watches actors or sheetMarkStore, so such a change shows only at the next ballot, setting or user connection.
findings.failure_scenario: Before sending the ballots a GM gives a student to another player in Foundry's ownership window; the vote window still names the old player among those who would get a ballot.
findings.expected: The vote window hears actors, as the GM panel's Students window does.
findings.refutation_tried: The primary reads the participants again at Send (vote.mjs:645-652 comment; ballotFor), so the ballots go right; only the list on screen is old.
findings.probe: Open the vote window; change a student's owner; read `.drpg-vote-status` three seconds later.

findings.title: The console's case schema does not hear the trace ledger or the tokens: a trace placed during the trial, or an unfound one renamed on its card, keeps its node as drawn
findings.surface: the case schema in the console's slot - 'Case schema'
findings.what_happens: caseGraph builds the evidence nodes from remnantsOn (the ledger, remnantStore, over each scene's tokens). The schema's region watches items, four settings, four other stores and the chat hooks. A write that touches only the ledger or a token - a GM renaming an unfound trace on its Remnant card (no Truth Bullet copy, so no item write), a trace placed - redraws nothing.
findings.evidence:
case-trial.mjs:126         watch: { items: true, settings: [SETTINGS.trialQueue, SETTINGS.clock, SETTINGS.murderState, SETTINGS.trialProgress], stores: [caseTickStore, caseSchemaStore, keyPlanStore, blackenedStore], hooks: ["createChatMessage", "updateChatMessage", "deleteChatMessage"] },
case-schema.mjs:373         for (const token of remnantsOn(scene)) {
findings.failure_scenario: During the trial a GM corrects the name of a trace nobody found on its Remnant card; the schema in the console keeps the old name on its node.
findings.expected: remnantStore among the schema's stores, as the dashboard's region has it.
findings.refutation_tried: A reshape ruling posts and updates chat cards, which the schema hears, so that road redraws it; a Remnant card edit of a found trace writes its copies (items), which it hears too. Left: ledger-only writes.
findings.probe: Console open in a trial; set an unfound trace's public name through `game.drpg` or its card; read the node's label in `.drpg-case-trial-live`.
